items.title: Police find human remains during search for missing teen
items.description: Detectives are investigating after human remains were found during a search for a missing teenage girl in Victoria's west.

items.title: Telstra's returning CEO Vicki Brady 'deeply sorry' for national outage
items.description: Telstra chief executive Vicki Brady apologises to the company's customers, saying the telco let them down and that investigations into the cause of Wednesday's Telstra outage are continuing.

items.title: First native bird found with H5 bird flu, marking 'devastating' new reality
items.description: CSIRO lab testing has confirmed the detection of H5 bird flu in a greater crested tern — the first time the strain has been detected in an Australian seabird, after previous confirmed cases involved migratory birds from the sub-Antarctic region.

items.title: Derryn Hinch remembered as courageous but provocative crusader for justice
items.description: Media identity Derryn Hinch is being remembered as a provocative but courageous journalist who was ahead of his time in his fight against institutional sex abuse.

items.title: X under fire for 'shocking disrespect' of antisemitism royal commission
items.description: Social media giants, including Elon Musk's X Corp, have come under fire with the royal commission on antisemitism expressing frustration at platforms' refusal to engage.

items.title: Australia's huntsman fastest spider on record, new study suggests
items.description: A species of huntsman spider found in Queensland is the fastest mover out of more than 250 spider species analysed in a new study.

items.title: Eight charged over alleged plot to kill Trump, Musk and Netanyahu at UFC fight
items.description: Eight men have been accused of planning a drone and shooting attack that aimed to kill the US president and SpaceX founder at the UFC Freedom 250 event held at the White House in June.

items.title: Australian woman accused of illegally voting in US faces jury trial
items.description: A Sydney woman will face trial in the US state of Louisiana after being accused of falsely claiming to be a US citizen and voting illegally in two federal elections.

items.title: Economist Justin Wolfers on the 'absurdity' of Trump's America
items.description: Former Reserve Bank economist Justin Wolfers says Australia urgently needs to consider the role of money in its politics while examining how US President Donald Trump profits from his position.

items.title: Australian-first CO2-powered battery planned for coal town
items.description: The Victorian government unveils a plan to build a compressed CO2 battery storage system in the heart of the state's coal country.

items.title: Not only is the Iran war not over, it is at a dangerous inflection point
items.description: Not only is the war not over, it is once again at a dangerous inflection point, as the US and Iran revert to military options to deal with differences over their interim peace agreement.

items.title: This Place: Boonoo Moodla
items.description: Boonoo Moodla, Billy Lights Point, has been a place of gathering and fishing for the Barngarla people for thousands of years. As part of NAIDOC Week the ABC is looking at Indigenous peoples' connection to country, and what makes it so special. NAIDOC Week is marking 50 years of Deadly and runs from July 5 until July 12.

items.title: Police slide into DMs of underworld group chat with warning
items.description: An encrypted phone network allegedly used by Sydney's underworld to orchestrate murders, kidnappings and drug deals has been infiltrated by NSW Police after they arrested a trio accused of running the "VIP Network".

items.title: Australia's most played song on radio this week draws AI criticisms
items.description: A cover of the Madonna hit Like a Prayer is at the top of the charts but criticisms have been levied at the artist behind the cover, Josh Fawaz, over his suspected use of artificial intelligence.

items.title: The Rolling Stones prove 'This never gets old!' with new album
items.description: On album #25, Foreign Tongues, rock's elder statesmen once again dismantle concerns whether men in their eighties can still make great records.

items.title: A guide to choosing the right potato for any meal you're making
items.description: Potatoes are undeniably versatile and tasty but choosing which variety to buy has never been more complicated. Brushed or washed? Yellow, white or pink? Mashing or roasting? And now there are low-carb spuds too.

items.title: The lowdown on lush native lawns that only need mowing once a year
items.description: If mowing the lawn is getting you down, it might be time to ditch your exotic buffalo, couch or kikuyu grass and switch to a native alternative.

items.title: Cattle farmer plants 14,000 trees to help slow flow of flood water
items.description: Jeff Imeson has planted around 14,000 trees on his property near Nimbin in a bid to help slow the flow of future floods.

items.title: Musician loses discrimination fight against orchestra over Gaza comments
items.description: The unlawful discrimination case brought by Jayson Gillham against the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra sprung from the orchestra's decision to cancel his scheduled performance over comments he made about Gaza.

items.title: Regulator closes 45 family day care residences across Melbourne
items.description: For the first time, Victoria's Early Childhood Regulatory Authority has used its powers to suspend a childcare operator, closing 45 family day care residences across Melbourne.

items.title: Brisbane Airport flight paths altered following noise review
items.description: People living in areas such as Redcliffe, southern Moreton Bay, Bribie Island and Logan are set to benefit the most, but there will be no change to the flight path over Bulimba.

items.title: Traditional owners say Noongar settlement ignores their rights
items.description: Traditional owners from WA's Wheatbelt say a historic native title settlement has increased division among Noongar groups.

items.title: The meteorite at the centre of a 'culture war' between the UK and Australia
items.description: The fight to claim a 3.5-tonne space rock didn't just kickstart a publicity battle that divided an empire — it also left a gaping hole in culture. Centuries on, the question remains: Who owned it?

items.title: The 'stunt' that could cost UK far right leader Nigel Farage his political career
items.description: Nigel Farage is facing intensifying scrutiny over his finances and millions of dollars' worth of donations. Here's how he got here.

items.title: Charlie Kirk's family requests evidence against accused killer be released
items.description: The family of conservative activist Charlie Kirk has pleaded with a judge to allow more public access to evidence presented against the man accused of the assassination.
